answer: Anchor each agent identity to a cedar-like root: a hardware-attested key that must complete a stream of useful, verifiable tasks before it can transact. Each completed task emits a signed receipt, and the receipts form a plume of evidence that peers can check without trusting the agent. Reputation then ripples outward only through real counterparties who stake on the work they received, so a Sybil farm must pay the full cost of genuine work for every fake identity — thousands of verified task-hours per sockpuppet — while honest agents accumulate standing by doing the same work once.
